market: JCI fell 0.78% to 6,172, tracking Nasdaq's 1.34% drop and VIX spike to 17.49.
USD/IDR weakened to 17,700 as DXY rose 0.69%, pressuring foreign flows.
economic: BI hiked 25 bp to 5.75%, totaling 1% in a month, to defend the rupiah.
Brent crude fell 1.29% and coal proxy ITMG dropped 1.33%, while nickel proxy INCO gained 2.71%.
tech_ai: Waymo recalled 4,000 robotaxis over highway construction zone risks.
Railway secured $100 million for AI-native cloud infrastructure to challenge AWS.
political: Prabowo emphasized strategic partnership with Germany to face global challenges.
US-Iran peace deal and Intel-Apple chip partnership may shift foreign flows toward defensive cyclicals.

arbiter_brief: The JCI's 0.78% decline reflects a triple squeeze from Wall Street risk-off, a stronger dollar, and BI's 25 bp hike to 5.75%. Nasdaq's 1.34% drop and VIX surge signal tech valuation spillover, pressuring domestic tech and foreign outflows. USD/IDR at 17,700 despite the hike suggests market doubts BI can anchor the rupiah against DXY at 100.78. Coal fell on Brent's slide, but nickel rose on supply optimism. Higher cost of capital from BI's cumulative 1% hike chokes early-stage tech and climate financing. Expect continued foreign net selling until rupiah stabilizes below 17,600.
executive_brief: Hedge against rupiah weakness as BI's 1% cumulative hike fails to anchor USD/IDR below 17,600.
Shift portfolio toward nickel and defensive cyclicals; avoid tech and coal amid foreign outflow risk.
Prepare for higher cost of capital choking early-stage venture and climate project financing in Indonesia.

sectors.name: Technology
sectors.ai: Indonesia tech underperformed US peers, dragged by broad selloff, but BELI's +2.70% signals selective resilience. Focus on BELI's structural growth in digital infrastructure and WIFI's connectivity demand as defensive plays; avoid GOTO/BUKA until monetization visibility improves.
themes: Digital infrastructure capex in Indonesia remains a durable driver as BELI and WIFI expand fiber and data center capacity to meet rising internet penetration and cloud adoption.
Monetization challenges for Indonesian e-commerce and fintech platforms (GOTO, BUKA) persist due to price-sensitive consumers and regulatory pressures, capping near-term upside.
US tech rate sensitivity continues to spill over into Indonesian tech valuations, but local names with tangible asset bases (BELI, WIFI) offer relative insulation from global volatility.

macro_analysis.point: Bank Indonesia's 25 bp rate hike to 5.75% (totaling 100 bp in a month) was explicitly aimed at defending the rupiah, but the USD/IDR only strengthened 0.27% while JCI fell 0.78%, indicating the market sees the move as insufficient to stem capital outflows given the hawkish Fed signal and rising US yields (10Y +3.5 bp). The divergence between BI's tightening and persistent rupiah weakness suggests foreign investors remain skeptical, pressuring JCI via financials (-0.65%) and rate-sensitive tech (-1.94%).

The US-Iran deal taking effect (VIDEO 8) triggered a 1.29% drop in Brent crude and 1.82% in WTI, which should benefit Indonesia's net oil import position and support rupiah stability, but the positive commodity tailwind was overwhelmed by the broader risk-off sentiment from Fed hawkishness and rising US yields. Coal proxy ITMG fell 1.33% despite lower oil, as the global growth scare from higher rates outweighed energy substitution narratives.

Japan's rate hike to a 31-year high (NEWS 9) adds to the global tightening impulse, strengthening the yen and pressuring carry trades that had funded Indonesian assets, contributing to the 1.34% Nasdaq decline as tech valuations compress. This cross-market tightening cycle is particularly damaging for Indonesia's duration-sensitive tech sector (-1.94%) and property (-1.55%), as higher global rates reduce the attractiveness of emerging market yield plays.

The key risk to watch is whether BI's cumulative 100 bp hike will be enough to stabilize the rupiah ahead of the June RDG, or if further tightening is needed as the Fed signals more hikes (NEWS 7). If USD/IDR breaches 17,700, foreign outflows from JCI could accelerate, particularly in financials and consumer sectors, while commodity names like INCO (+2.71% today) may offer a temporary haven if nickel demand holds.
